question: Universal Containers wants to store Payment Term Details on the Account object, but the fields should only be visible on certain record types and for certain user profiles. How can a System Administrator quickly determine which user profiles, page layouts, and record types include certain fields?
optionA: Log in as each user profile and view the Account Page Layouts.
optionB: Use the Field Accessibility Viewer for the fields in question
optionC: Universally require the field at the field level.
optionD: Click the Field-Level Security for the field on each Profile.
explanation:
Using the Field Accessibility Viewer for the fields in question is how the administrator quickly determines this. It shows, in a single matrix, which profiles, record types, and page layouts expose a field as visible, hidden, or read-only, making it the fastest way to audit field exposure.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Log in as each user profile and view the Account Page Layouts) — slow, one profile at a time, and it does not show record-type or FLS detail directly.
Option C (Universally require the field at the field level) — changes the field's behaviour and is irrelevant to auditing where it appears.
Option D (Click the Field-Level Security for the field on each Profile) — one profile at a time, and it omits the page-layout and record-type dimensions.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.checking_field_accessibility_for_a_particular_field.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has implemented a community for its customers using the Customer Community sense type. They have implemented a custom object to store service requests that has a look up to the account record. The Organization Wide Default External Access for the service request object is set to Private. Universal Containers wants their customers to be able to see service requests for their account through the community. Customers should not see service requests for other accounts. What Salesforce feature can the Architect use to implement this?
optionA: Use manual sharing to share the service requests manually when a new community user is added.
optionB: Use a Sharing Set to share service requests related to the account based on the community user's profile.
optionC: Use a Sharing Rule to share service requests to the community user based on their role.
optionD: Use Apex Managed Sharing to share service requests related to the account to the appropriate community users.
explanation:
Using a Sharing Set to share service requests related to the account based on the community user's profile is the feature to use. Customer Community users have no roles, so a Sharing Set keyed on the service request's lookup to the user's Account grants each customer access to their account's service requests and nothing else.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (manual sharing when a new community user is added) — per record and per user; it does not scale and misses requests created after the user was added.
Option C (a Sharing Rule based on the community user's role) — Customer Community users have no roles, so there is nothing for a rule to target.
Option D (Apex Managed Sharing) — unnecessary code for a case the declarative Sharing Set covers exactly.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_setting_light_users.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_license_types_communities.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has set the Org-Wide Sharing Default for Accounts to Private and has created some sharing rules to extend access based on certain data access policies. An architect has been asked to review access to a certain set of key customer accounts. How might this review be conducted?
optionA: Export the Account Share table and review.
optionB: Run a Report on Sharing in the Admin Console.
optionC: Log in as each user and Run the All Accounts List View.
optionD: Use the Sharing button on each customer Account.
explanation:
Exporting the Account Share table and reviewing it is how the review might be conducted. To audit who has access to a specific set of accounts under a Private model with sharing rules, export and inspect the AccountShare table, which lists every share row and its row cause.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Run a Report on Sharing in the Admin Console) — there is no built-in sharing report in an admin console.
Option C (Log in as each user and run the All Accounts list view) — one user at a time, and it shows what a user sees rather than why; it does not scale to a set of accounts.
Option D (Use the Sharing button on each customer Account) — one record at a time; it does not scale to a set of accounts and cannot be exported for review.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_bulk_sharing_understanding.htm
https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_record_access_under_the_hood.pdf

question: Universal Containers has a custom Job object with a private sharing model. Based on the size and location of the Job, different teams must have access to edit the specific Job record. To support this requirement, Apex Managed Sharing has been implemented to share records with the required users. Since the teams change frequently, managed sharing recalculations need to be manually run frequently. What can the Architect do to optimize this process?
optionA: Change the sharing model on the Job object to Public Read/Write.
optionB: Create a scheduled job to automatically run the sharing recalculations on a nightly basis.
optionC: Create public groups for each team, and share the jobs with the groups instead of users.
optionD: Create a custom Visualforce page to edit the jobs and specify Without Sharing on the controller.
explanation:
Creating public groups for each team and sharing the jobs with the groups instead of users is what the Architect can do. Because the teams change frequently, sharing each job to a per-team public group means you only update group membership, which avoids recalculating record shares, instead of recalculating shares to individual users.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Change the sharing model to Public Read/Write) — removes the security the private model exists to provide.
Option B (a scheduled job to run the sharing recalculations nightly) — still incurs the full recalculation cost every night, and leaves access stale during the day.
Option D (a Visualforce page with Without Sharing on the controller) — bypasses record security entirely for anyone using the page.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.user_groups.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_bulk_sharing_understanding.htm

question: Universal Containers has a Private Sharing Model for the Opportunity object. Sales Rep A at Universal Containers created the Opportunity record and then transferred ownership of the Opportunity record to Sales Rep B. Both Sales Rep A and B have the same role in the Role Hierarchy. What access will Sales Rep A have to the Opportunity after the transfer?
optionA: Full Access
optionB: No Access
optionC: Read/Write
optionD: Read Only
explanation:
No Access is what Sales Rep A will have to the Opportunity after the transfer. Under a Private model, same-role peers do not see each other's records, and the prior owner's access ends at the transfer.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Full Access) — only the owner has full access, and Rep A is no longer the owner.
Option C (Read/Write) — nothing grants the former owner write access; there is no share row left behind by a transfer.
Option D (Read Only) — a Private OWD grants no read to peers, and the same role confers nothing between its members.
References:
https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_record_access_under_the_hood.pdf
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has just deployed a change to its role hierarchy. A manager is reporting that their staff can now see Accounts that they do not own and should not have access to. How should the Architect troubleshoot?
optionA: While logged in as the System Administrator, use the Field Accessibility Viewer to view a matrix of who has access to Accounts.
optionB: While logged in as the one of the Staff members, navigate to a sample account and use the Sharing button to determine who has access.
optionC: While logged in as the one of the Staff members, navigate to their user record and inspect their profile and role membership.
optionD: While logged in as the System Administrator, review the organization-wide default settings for the Account object under Sharing Settings.
explanation:
Logging in as one of the Staff members, navigating to a sample account and using the Sharing button to determine who has access is how the Architect should troubleshoot. It lists every user and group with access to that specific record together with the row cause, which names the exact mechanism — role hierarchy, sharing rule, or team — that granted it.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the Field Accessibility Viewer as System Administrator) — reports on field-level security and says nothing about record access.
Option C (inspect the staff member's profile and role membership) — shows what the user is, not why one record reached them.
Option D (review the organization-wide default settings for Account) — describes the baseline for all Accounts and cannot explain access to a particular one.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.granting_access_to_records_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.managing_the_sharing_model.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: After setting up Customer Community and enabling collaboration, the architect realizes that customers can only see Chatter posts from other customers in their account. What should the architect do to allow viewing Chatter posts from all customers?
optionA: Enable Community User Visibility.
optionB: Set View All for Chatter posts.
optionC: Enable Chatter Super User.
optionD: Enable Internal Users Visibility.
explanation:
Enabling Community User Visibility is what the architect should do. What the customers are experiencing is the default, and the setting that widens it is Site User Visibility. Salesforce separates the two behaviours: Portal User Visibility means "portal users in the same customer or partner portal account can see each other", which is precisely the "only people in my own account" symptom; Site User Visibility "controls whether user sharing is available for authenticated users in your org's sites", and enabling it exposes the per-site option "See other members of this site".
So turning on site (community) user visibility is what lets customers see one another — and therefore each other's Chatter posts — beyond their own account. Both settings apply only when the org-wide external default for the User object is Private; if it is Public Read Only, all users already see each other regardless.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Set View All for Chatter posts) — there is no "View All for Chatter posts" setting.
Option C (Enable Chatter Super User) — not the mechanism; super user access concerns partner record visibility, not who can see whom in a site.
Option D (Enable Internal Users Visibility) — governs a different direction of the relationship, whether site users can see internal users.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_user_sharing.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers provides 24x7 support for its customers worldwide using call centers in three different countries with each one covering an 8-hour shift in different time zones. Service reps in a call center have access to the same information but only during their local working hours. Which feature in Salesforce controls access for specific login hours?
optionA: Set the login hours on user records
optionB: Permission sets
optionC: Custom permissions
optionD: Profiles
explanation:
Profiles are the feature that controls access for specific login hours. Login hours that restrict when users can access Salesforce are configured on the Profile, so each call center's profile limits access to its local shift.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Set the login hours on user records) — login hours are not a user-record setting.
Option B (Permission sets) — permission sets do not carry login hours.
Option C (Custom permissions) — custom permissions are flags that Apex, flows and validation rules can check; they do not restrict login times.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.login_hours.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has 200 distributors that use Partner Community licenses. Partners cannot see each other's data, but UC is also trying to give more visibility to data for certain individuals at a distributor. HOW can an Architect give users in the partner user role access to all Case and Container records owned by any user, regardless of role, at the same distributor?
optionA: Create an ownership-based sharing rule.
optionB: Create sharing sets.
optionC: Create a Permission Set granting "View All" permission to Case and Container records.
optionD: Give super user permission to the individual partner users.
explanation:
Giving super user permission to the individual partner users is the intended mechanism and the only option here that scales, because it is granted per user rather than configured per distributor. But read its scope carefully, because this item overreaches. Grant Portal Super User Access documents that a super user reaches "records of other partner users who are at their role level or below them in the account role hierarchy", and each partner account carries a Partner Executive > Partner Manager > Partner User hierarchy. A super user in the Partner User role therefore reaches only other Partner User-role records - not the records owned by the partner managers and executives above them.
So the stem's "any user, regardless of role" is not what this option delivers, and no other option delivers it either. Treat the item as defective in its stem, with D as the best available answer.
One detail in D's favour: super user access applies "only to cases, leads, custom objects, and opportunities", which does cover both Case and the custom Container object this question asks about.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Create an ownership-based sharing rule) — would need one rule per distributor across 200 accounts.
Option B (Create sharing sets) — grant portal users access through account and contact relationships rather than lifting a partner role restriction.
Option C (a Permission Set granting "View All" on Case and Container) — would expose every case and container in the org rather than one distributor's.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_partner_super_user_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_partner_roles_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has created a custom Sales Operations profile with read and edit access to the Category field on a custom object. There is a new requirement that 3 of the 100 users assigned to the Sales Operations Profile should have read-only access to the Category field. How can the Architect support this request? Choose one answer.
optionA: Create a permission set in the Category field to read-only and assign it to the users.
optionB: Create a new profile without edit access to Category and assign it to the users.
optionC: Create a new page layout with the Category Field set to read-only for these users.
optionD: Create a custom permission to grant read-only access to Category and assign it to the users.
explanation:
Creating a new profile without edit access to Category and assigning it to the three users is how the Architect supports this. Field-Level Security through permission sets is additive, meaning it can only add access as a union and cannot remove the profile's existing edit access, so the only way to give three users read-only is a profile that does not grant edit on the field.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a permission set with the Category field read-only) — the source's answer, but a permission set cannot subtract the edit access the profile already grants.
Option C (a new page layout with Category read-only for these users) — a read-only layout does not enforce FLS; the field stays editable through the API, list views and other layouts.
Option D (a custom permission granting read-only access) — custom permissions do not control field-level security.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_field_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
Sales manager at universal containers (UC) have requested viewing customer invoices in Salesforce. Invoice data is mastered in the ERP system. The architect at UC decided to surface the customer invoices in salesforce using external objects and did the following:
- Configured an external object called Invoice.
- Created a lookup relationship between account and the invoice.
How can the architect grant the sales managers access to the customer invoices data?
optionA: By creating sharing rules to share the invoices records with users in sales mangers roles.
optionB: By creating manual sharing to share invoices with relevant sales managers.
optionC: By creating controlling the invoices object permission on the sales manager's profile.
optionD: By creating a sharing set to share invoices with users in sales manager role.
explanation:
Controlling the Invoice object permission on the sales manager's profile is how the architect grants access. For an external object with a lookup to Account, access is granted through the object-level permission on the profile, because sharing rules, sharing sets, and manual sharing do not apply to external objects.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (sharing rules to share invoice records with sales manager roles) — sharing rules do not apply to external objects; the rows are not stored in Salesforce.
Option B (manual sharing of invoices with sales managers) — external object records cannot be manually shared.
Option D (a sharing set to share invoices with the sales manager role) — sharing sets are for Experience Cloud site users, and do not apply to external objects in any case.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.salesforce_connect.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: (Variant) Sales Operations at Universal Containers (UC) wants to create list views to filter opportunities for certain geographies. In which two ways can UC hide list views that are not relevant to an individual user since there will be many list views? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Share the list views with the appropriate queue.
optionB: Share the list views with the appropriate individual users.
optionC: Share the list views with the appropriate public group.
optionD: Share the list views with the appropriate role in the role hierarchy
explanation:
Sharing the list views with the appropriate public group, and sharing them with the appropriate role in the role hierarchy, are the two ways. List views are shown or hidden by their sharing target, and Salesforce describes the available choices as "All Users, Only Me, or Groups of Users" — where groups of users covers public groups and roles, including roles and subordinates. Pointing each geography's view at the matching group or role keeps a user's list-view picker down to what is relevant to them.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Share the list views with the appropriate queue) — queues are not a list-view sharing target.
Option B (Share the list views with individual users) — "sharing a List View with a specific individual user is not natively supported", and the documented workaround is to wrap that user in a public group, which is option C by another route.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000387584&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.user_groups.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: At Universal Containers, Accounts and Contacts are normally visible to all employees, and Proposals (custom object) are visible to the Account owner and managers. However, some Proposals are considered confidential and are managed by a Strategic Proposals team. These Proposals should not be visible to anyone in the Sales group other than the owner and the strategic team. How should the architect design for this requirement?
optionA: Proposal Owner set to the Strategic Deals Team Queue and set the Account relationship to Master-Detail.
optionB: Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies and set an Owner-Based Sharing rule for Strategic Deals team.
optionC: Proposal Owner set to the Strategic Deals Team Queue and create an owner-based sharing rule to grant visibility to the Account owner
optionD: Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies and set a Criteria-Based Sharing rule for Strategic Deals team.
explanation:
Disabling Grant Access Using Hierarchies and setting an Owner-Based Sharing rule for the Strategic Deals team is how the architect should design this. Confidential proposals must be hidden from the wider Sales group, including managers above the owner, so switch off the hierarchy roll-up on Proposals, then use an owner-based sharing rule to grant the Strategic Proposals team access. Note that disabling the hierarchy globally is in tension with normal proposals remaining visible to managers.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Owner set to the Strategic Deals Team Queue and a Master-Detail to Account) — master-detail would make proposals Controlled by Parent, and Accounts are visible to everyone, so the confidential proposals would be exposed rather than isolated.
Option C (Owner set to the Queue plus an owner-based rule to the Account owner) — queue ownership does not remove the records from the hierarchy roll-up, so managers above the account owner would still see them.
Option D (Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies and a Criteria-Based Sharing rule) — would require a flag field to key on and is less direct than sharing what the strategic team owns.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: Universal Containers wants to create a way to store sensitive Invoice Data in Salesforce. A User who owns an Account should not see every Invoice, but only invoices that they or their subordinates own. Which two features should be considered during this solution implementation? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Deploy the Relationship between Accounts and the Invoices Object as Master-Detail.
optionB: Ensure that the Organization-Wide Default sharing for Invoices is set to Private.
optionC: Create a Workflow that populates the Invoice sharing object upon Insert.
optionD: Deploy the Relationship between Accounts and the Invoices Object as Lookup.
explanation:
Ensuring the Organization-Wide Default for Invoices is Private, and deploying the Account-to-Invoice relationship as a Lookup, are the two features to consider. Owner-or-subordinates visibility requires the Role Hierarchy on a Private object, so the Invoice OWD must be Private and the relationship must be a Lookup so invoices have their own owner and sharing.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Master-Detail between Accounts and Invoices) — would force Controlled-by-Parent and could not be Private, contradicting the requirement; the source pairing of A and B is internally inconsistent.
Option C (a Workflow that populates the Invoice sharing object upon Insert) — workflow cannot create share records, and the hierarchy already provides owner-or-subordinate visibility on a Private object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_manytomany.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
Universal Containers has the following Sharing Settings for their Org:
Account = Private.
Contact = Controlled by Parent.
Opportunity = Private.
Case = Private.
They have enabled "Default Account Teams" and have trained users to set up their Default Team. Which three access levels can be set on the Account Team Member? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Opportunity Access
optionB: Case Access
optionC: Contact Access
optionD: Contract Access
explanation:
Opportunity Access, Case Access, and Account Access are the three access levels that can be set on the Account Team Member. Access can be set for the Account itself and for child objects whose OWD is below Public Read/Write, here Opportunity and Case, both Private.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option C (Contact Access) — Contact is Controlled by Parent, so it has no separate access setting.
Option D (Contract Access) — there is no Contract Access option on account teams.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.accountteam_def.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Partner users can access records belonging to users in their account at their same role or lower in the role hierarchy, for Cases, Leads, Opportunities and Custom Objects. Which of the following access has to be given?
optionA: Delegated External User Administrator
optionB: A sharing set granting access through the account
optionC: View All permission on each object
optionD: Partner Super User permission
explanation:
The Partner Super User permission is the access that has to be given. It is what lets a partner user reach Cases, Leads, Opportunities, and custom object records owned by other users in their own account at the same role or below in the hierarchy.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Delegated External User Administrator) — grants the ability to manage other external users, not to see their records.
Option B (A sharing set granting access through the account) — sharing sets apply to Customer Community licences that have no role hierarchy, which is precisely the mechanism this question is not describing.
Option C (View All permission on each object) — would expose every record of the object org-wide, far beyond the account-scoped access required.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_partner_super_user_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_partner_roles_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has recently implemented an integration that is populating 50 custom fields on the account object. They would like these fields to be available to Managers for reporting but do not want them to clutter the page layouts. What should the Architect recommend as a solution?
optionA: Add the fields to the Managers' Account Page Layout; mark the page layout section as Collapsed.
optionB: Grant the Managers access to the fields using a Role-Based Sharing Rule; leave them hidden on the page layout.
optionC: Add the fields to a Custom Report; grant the Managers' Role access to the report folder.
optionD: Grant Managers access to the fields using Field-Level Security; do not add them to a page layout.
explanation:
Granting Managers access to the fields using Field-Level Security and not adding them to a page layout is the recommendation. Managers need the 50 fields for reporting but not on layouts, and reporting reads FLS rather than layouts, so the fields can be left off the page entirely.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (add the fields to the layout in a Collapsed section) — a collapsed section still clutters the layout and is one click from expanding.
Option B (a Role-Based Sharing Rule, hidden on the layout) — sharing rules control record access, not field visibility; without FLS the fields are invisible in reports too.
Option C (a Custom Report with folder access for the Managers' role) — a report does not grant the underlying FLS; fields the profile cannot read do not appear in it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_field_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Corporate Identity and Access Team needs to audit User setup in the Salesforce. What two permissions should be granted to this team so they can perform their audit? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: View permission on the User object
optionB: View Setup and Configuration
optionC: View All Users
optionD: View All Data
explanation:
View Setup and Configuration, and View All Users, are the two permissions to grant. Auditing user setup requires View Setup and Configuration to inspect setup and View All Users to see every user record.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (View permission on the User object) — narrower and not the audit permission; it does not open Setup.
Option D (View All Data) — over-grants beyond the scope of a user-setup audit, exposing every record in the org.

question: Assuming Person Account is enabled in a Salesforce organization, which three objects can be configured as "Controlled by Parent" in Sharing Settings? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Opportunity
optionB: Order
optionC: Asset
optionD: Contact
explanation:
Order, Asset, and Contact are the three objects that can be configured as Controlled by Parent. With Person Accounts enabled, those are the objects that can be set to Controlled by Parent relative to their parent account.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Opportunity) — has its own OWD and is not a Controlled-by-Parent option.
Option E (Case) — likewise has its own OWD and is not a Controlled-by-Parent option.
